text.p: Bridgestone/Firestone Inc said Wednesday first half sales and earnings exceeded estimates.

The company, the largest wholly owned subsidiary of Bridgestone Corp, also projected net income for the full year of $200 million on sales of $7.0 billion, noting this compares to 1996 earnings of $172 million on sales of $6.5 billion.

For the first half, the company reported net income of $101.3 million on sales of $3.39 billion. Profits not only topped higher than the estimated $84.6 million, but also exceeded 1996's first half net of $95 million, it noted.
The company said first half sales were estimated to be $3.33 billion.

Bridgestone/Firestone chief executive officer Masatoshi Ono said the results surpassed estimates for several reasons, including increased product visibility through the Indy car and Formula One racing efforts, the introduction of new products such as the Firestone FT70c passenger tire, the performance of non-tire businesses and improvements in markets outside the U.S.

"We are hopeful our market share and profitability will continue to improve," Ono said. "The essential elements for our success are in place, we just need to keep focused on helping the Bridgestone Corporation achieve a 20 percent share of the market by the year 2000.
"Looking at our growth in recent years, that is a totally realistic goal," he added.
Bridgestone now has 19 percent of the world tire market, spokesman Trevor Hoskins said.
